subject: Galileo-12B: spike in 502/504 timeouts — initial notice and follow-ups
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: BrightBridge Eng <eng@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-25T08:14:00Z
Subject: Galileo-12B: spike in 502/504 timeouts — initial notice

Hi Sara / BrightBridge eng team,

Quick heads-up: starting ~07:50 PDT we observed an elevated rate of 502/504 and other 5xx responses for requests routed to galileo-12b in us-west1. Error rate peaked at ~6% of requests for a ~35 minute window; some requests experienced long tail timeouts (30s+).

Impact:
- Affected routes: model=galileo-12b (default generation & chat endpoints)
- Customer-visible symptoms: intermittent generation failures and degraded streaming for some sessions
- Scope: primarily us-west1; small amount of traffic in us-east failed over normally

Immediate actions taken:
- Automated smart-routing shifted ~40% of traffic to galileo-12b-v2 (quantized variant) as a soft fallback.
- We increased instance reuse and reduced batching thresholds for galileo-12b to shorten tail latency while we investigate.
- Rate of failures has dropped but has not fully returned to baseline; our on-call is actively tracing kernel-level failures and network retries.

Attachments: brief logs and charts attached (diag_summary.pdf, rw_galileo12b_dump.log).

Planned next steps:
1) We will continue to route more traffic to the v2 fallback if the baseline does not stabilize in the next hour.
2) Ben and infra will follow up with a diagnostic snapshot and root-cause signals.
3) We can schedule a short bridge if you want live updates — suggested windows: 09:30 or 10:15 PDT.

I realize this is disruptive — apologies. I'll update you within the hour with progress and a clearer timeline.

Cheers,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Galileo-12B: spike in 502/504 timeouts — initial notice

Thanks — quick status from infra side:
- We believe the immediate cause is an interaction between a recent kernel selector change and longer sequence inputs causing KV-cache evictions under high-concurrency workloads. This led to transient OOM-like behaviors in a handful of containers and manifested as 502/504.
- Mitigation applied: rolled a hotfix patch to the selector on the galileo-12b pool and lowered max concurrent requests per worker to reduce contention.
- Observed effect: error rate down from 6% to ~1.2% over the last 12 minutes; tail latencies improving.

Next steps:
- We'll keep galileo-12b-v2 as the primary fallback for the next 6 hours.
- Collecting full heap/dump from impacted workers; attaching a trimmed dump to the ticket (rw_galileo12b_dump.log).
- Postmortem owners: infra (Ben) + runtime (Marissa). ETA for root cause writeup: 24–48 hours depending on dump analysis.

If BrightBridge wants a post-incident call I can join with Marissa.

-ben

Sara — quick update following the hotfix and routing changes:

What we did since my last note:
- Applied a selector patch that prevents aggressive KV eviction on long sequences.
- Reduced per-worker concurrency to lower contention for a rolling window.
- Kept galileo-12b-v2 as fallback; no config change required on your side.

Current status:
- Error rate stabilized to ~0.9% for the last 45 minutes.
- No data loss; retry/backoff behavior preserved.

Recommended action for BrightBridge:
- If you continue to see rare failures, please enable client-side 5xx retry with exponential backoff (we recommend 3 retries, jitter).
- We recommend pinning critical flows to galileo-12b-v2 for the next 24 hours if you want maximum stability; we can do this via a routing override for your tenant.

Would you like a 30-minute bridge at 14:00 PDT to walk through what happened and next steps? If so, I'll send an invite.

Thanks for bearing with us.

— Tessa

Subject: Galileo-12B — post-incident summary and immediate action items

Hi Sara and team,

Thank you for your patience while we completed initial diagnostics. Attached is a concise post-incident summary (diag_summary.pdf) and the trimmed dump we pulled from an impacted worker (rw_galileo12b_dump.log). Below are the key findings and the actions we are taking:

Executive summary:
- Root cause: a recent kernel-selector change increased the chance of KV-cache eviction for long-sequence requests under high concurrency. Some containers experienced transient resource exhaustion which led to 502/504 responses (~6% peak).
- Impact window: 2028-04-25T07:50–08:25 PDT.
- Mitigation: hotfix to selector logic, reduced concurrency limits, and temporary routing to galileo-12b-v2.

Action items and timeline:
1) Production hardening (INFRA-2345) — infra team to roll a guarded selector that accounts for variable sequence length distributions. ETA: 3 business days.
2) Improved observability — add a KV-eviction metric and per-model eviction dashboards. ETA: 5 business days.
3) Client-side guidance — we will publish a KB note with recommended retry/backoff settings and a routing override recipe for pinning fallbacks. ETA: 48 hours.
4) Postmortem write-up — full postmortem with timeline, RCA, and follow-ups to be posted to the ticket. Owners: Ben (infra) / Marissa (runtime). ETA: 48 hours for draft, 7 days for final.

Temporary support offer: if BrightBridge prefers, we can schedule a dedicated routing override for your tenant for the next 72 hours at no charge while we complete the hardening work.

Attachments: diag_summary.pdf (3 pages), rw_galileo12b_dump.log (trimmed).
